headline: Three-run eighth lifts Phillies past Brewers, 6-4
recap: The Phillies beat the Milwaukee Brewers 6-4 at Citizens Bank Park on Tuesday night, breaking a 3-3 tie with a three-run eighth inning. Bryson Stott walked and scored on Brandon Marsh's two-run homer in the second, and Alec Bohm's double drove in Trea Turner in the third to make it 3-0. Milwaukee answered with a William Contreras sacrifice fly in the fourth and pulled even in the sixth when Contreras singled home two more runs. Philadelphia went back ahead in the eighth: Stott's single scored Luis Arraez, Alec Bohm came around on a throwing error by center fielder Garrett Mitchell, and Marsh's RBI double brought in Stott. Luis Lara's single off closer Jhoan Duran scored Christian Yelich in the ninth for Milwaukee's final run. Zack Wheeler struck out 11 over 5.2 innings but did not factor in the decision, Jose Alvarado picked up the win with a scoreless relief out, and Duran worked around the ninth-inning run for his 33rd save.

The win was Philadelphia's second in a row, improving the Phillies to 87-70. They sit second in the NL East, 5.0 games behind the first-place Braves (92-65). The Marlins (77-80), Nationals (74-84) and Mets (72-85) follow.

The Phillies continue their series with Milwaukee on Wednesday at Citizens Bank Park, with Aaron Nola set to face Brewers right-hander Logan Henderson. First pitch is scheduled for 6:40 PM ET. Milwaukee is favored at -144 on the moneyline, with Philadelphia at +119 and getting 1.5 runs on the run line.
